findings.location: frontend/tests/composables/useFunnelCanvas.spec.ts — 'maps model to nodes and edges' test
findings.issue: The forward-mapping test verifies entry-edge source node ids via 'start' and 'e.source !== start', but does NOT assert the event-trigger node id against the expected trigger-prefixed id (e.g. 'trigger:1'). A bug that uses an arbitrary id for the event-trigger node would pass the test because it only checks e.source !== 'start', not the exact id value.
findings.recommendation: Add: const evtEntry = findEdge(entryEdges, e => e.source !== 'start'); expect(evtEntry.source).toBe('trigger:1'); This pins the exact trigger node id contract.

findings.issue: The saved-node-only test calls connectEdge with targetStepId=null and expects a throw. This covers the null case, but the task TDD Anchor also requires testing that an edge to an unsaved (id==null) node in the graph is refused — i.e. connectEdge(f, ref, 'some-id-not-in-saved-set') throws. The second assertion (buildEdges with a next pointing at a missing id produces 0 edges) covers the forward pass, but the reverse-pass test only checks the null case, not the 'target exists as a step but id==null' case.
findings.recommendation: Add a connectEdge call with a targetStepId that is not null but does not appear in savedStepIds (e.g. 'not-saved'), assert it throws. This tests the saved-node-only constraint path in connectEdge line 506 separately from the null check.

findings.issue: The test disconnects each edge type separately from independent funnel snapshots. For the 'timeout' and 'button' disconnect cases, sibling fields are NOT explicitly checked. For afterTimeout, s[0].next and buttons are not asserted unchanged. For afterBtn, s[0].next and timeoutTargetStepId are not asserted unchanged. The tech-spec and TDD Anchor mandate: 'siblings unchanged' for every disconnect case.
findings.recommendation: After afterTimeout: add expect(afterTimeout.steps[0].next).toBe('s2'); expect(afterTimeout.steps[0].buttons![0].targetStepId).toBe('s2'). After afterBtn: add expect(afterBtn.steps[0].next).toBe('s2'); expect(afterBtn.steps[0].timeoutTargetStepId).toBe('s2'). Note: afterEntry sibling (steps) is also not explicitly checked.

findings.location: frontend/tests/composables/useFunnelCanvas.spec.ts:313 — 'degenerate graph falls back to grid placement'
findings.issue: The 'degenerate graph' test uses 10 disconnected step nodes (empty edges) and verifies finite coords. This does not actually exercise the dagre-throw fallback path — a forest of disconnected nodes is valid dagre input and dagre handles it correctly without throwing. The comment in the test acknowledges this. The fallback branch (grid placement) is tested only indirectly; there is no test that actually triggers a dagre exception to confirm the try/catch→gridLayout path works.
findings.recommendation: To truly exercise the fallback: mock dagre.layout to throw, or pass a graph with NaN-producing input, and assert finite coords result. Alternatively, the test name should be updated to 'lays out disconnected/orphan forest' to avoid implying the fallback is triggered. The current test is still useful for orphan forest coverage but does not fulfill the stated purpose.

findings.issue: The assertion 'payload.steps!.every(s => s.stepType !== undefined)' checks that every step has a stepType property, which is always true since step objects come from the model — this assertion would pass even if a note leaked into steps[] as long as that note object happened to have stepType defined. The actual guard 'some(s => s.text === "note A")' is meaningful, but the stepType check provides false confidence.
findings.recommendation: Replace the stepType check with: expect(payload.steps!.map(s => s.id)).toEqual(['s1']); — this is a concrete value assertion that directly tests notes isolation by checking that only the known step id is in steps[]. Alternatively: expect(payload.steps!.every(s => !('text' in s) || s.stepType !== undefined)) — but the id list is cleaner.

summary: 17 specs cover all 17 TDD anchor checklist items from the task. All critical paths have behavioral assertions: reverse-connect checks concrete field values AND sibling fields for next/button/timeout/entry; delete-node checks exact count=4 and names each nulled field by id; broken-edge checks named field+targetStepId strings; no-edge checks strict toBeNull() for all four edge types. Litmus test: removing core logic lines would break the assertions in all major tests — the tests are not mock-return or count-only. Five minor gaps found: (1) event-trigger node id not pinned with exact value in forward-mapping; (2) saved-node-only reverse-pass only tests null case, not non-saved-id case; (3) sibling-unchanged assertions missing for timeout and button disconnect cases; (4) degenerate-graph test does not actually trigger the dagre fallback branch; (5) stepType check in notes-isolation is weak. None are blockers. verdict=pass.
